researchQuestion: Do the three optimizer policies that remained nondominated under V3 shared repeated-mean validation remain nondominated relative to the three hand-designed baselines on a workload unseen to V3 search and finalist selection?

sourceEvidence.survivorRule: Include every optimizer policy on the shared-validation repeated-mean point-estimate Pareto front. Do not replace, cap, or reselect policies after observing holdout outcomes.

holdoutWorkload.selectionDisclosure: This pre-existing workload and its baseline-only V2 outcomes were known before this protocol. It was not used by V3 search, finalist selection, or shared validation. Results therefore test generalization beyond V3 training workloads but are not described as a fully blinded holdout.
holdoutWorkload.tailMetricLimitation: Each replay contains 24 Pods; linearly interpolated p95 depends on the 22nd and 23rd ordered observations and remains sensitive to a few upper-tail samples. Repeated policy-level means and uncertainty intervals are reported.

analysis.experimentalUnit: One fresh policy replay of the fixed 24-Pod mixed-burst holdout workload after scheduler rollout convergence and namespace cleanup.
primaryObjectives: Mean p95 scheduler-decision latency across the ten holdout repetitions.
Mean maximum workload-occupied worker nodes across the ten holdout repetitions.
analysis.primaryOutcome: Repeated-mean point-estimate Pareto membership of each frozen V3 survivor among all six policies on the holdout workload.
supportMetrics: 95% Student-t confidence intervals across ten independent repetition-level estimates
analysis.interpretation: Pareto dominance is computed from repeated-mean point estimates and is not a statistical significance test. Marginal confidence intervals quantify uncertainty but do not establish multivariate dominance.
analysis.validPositive: At least one frozen V3 survivor remains nondominated relative to all policies on the holdout repeated-mean point-estimate front, with every safety metric passing.
analysis.validNegative: No frozen V3 survivor remains nondominated, or the surviving count is lower than on shared validation. Preserve and report this outcome without replacing policies or redesigning the protocol.
analysis.claimBoundary: A survivor supports descriptive generalization to this fixed mixed-burst workload only. It does not establish statistical superiority, production generality, or superiority to the default Kubernetes scheduler.

execution.orderDecision: Rotate the policy that executes first by one position per repetition. Six repetitions form one complete position cycle; repetitions seven through ten repeat the first four rotations. This deterministic residual imbalance is committed before execution and no result-dependent reordering is allowed.
execution.estimatedWallTime: Approximately 34 minutes, with a one-hour operational allowance, linearly scaled from the completed V2 baseline-only holdout. This is a capacity estimate, not an observed V3 duration.
execution.failureRule: Any incomplete result, unschedulable Pod, missing timestamp, protocol drift, interruption, or restoration failure fails the official run. Preserve partial artifacts and do not replace or omit repetitions.
execution.postflightRule: Restore canonical weights and the normal 2s scheduler cadence, require a healthy one-replica scheduler deployment, verify four ready workers, and leave the evaluator namespace empty.
